context_excerpt: 2024-11-15 **Event**: On November 15, 2024, Governing Team A announced an adjustment to auto-parts tariff policy, allowing automakers to apply for an "offset" on tariffs paid on imported parts, up to a maximum of 3.75% of a vehicle's Country Y suggested retail price, dropping to 2.5% the following year. Administration A also set a Region L origin threshold: vehicles ensuring that 85% of parts are made in Country Y, C…

About a week after the cutoff (2024-11-22), in response to Country X's announcement that Person E2 the Vice Prime Minister would attend talks, and on the same day the central bank would lower the reserve requirement ratio and release about one trillion yuan, netizens would read Platform B as "negotiating with one hand and stabilizing the economy with the other." With confidence from the outside and back-up from the inside, the news of the RRR cut made stock bars shout that a bull market is coming.

About a week after the cutoff, on the eve of the negotiation, Leader A suddenly issued a document proposing to reduce the 145% of Country X to 80%. The spokesperson of Agency A added that 80% was a random number. The mainstream of Platform B would read it as Country Y first accept the soft bidding, and Country X sit firmly on Diaoyutai.

Within about a week after the cutoff, City G finished talking to Leader A on the first day, and Product C boasted of "major progress and comprehensive restart" while he himself went to play golf. Platform B would spoil the contrast, ridicule "major progress on the lips, 18 holes underfoot", and raise questions about his unilateral optimistic propaganda.

About two weeks after the cutoff, in response to Leader A's announcement in Agency A that Country X "agreed to remove non-tariff barriers" but was vague about it, Platform B netizens' first reaction was to be suspicious, reminding them to "listen to their words but also to watch their actions", thinking that Country X has not officially confirmed it, so don't agree for others.

Within about two weeks after the cutoff, Leader A cut tariffs on Country X from 145% to 30% for only 90 days. Platform B The mainstream stock market will unreservedly hail the trade war as completely over, with overwhelming confidence. Almost no one mentioned the hidden concern that "90 days is just a temporary arrangement."

About a month after the cutoff, in response to Leader A's admission that signing dozens of agreements in three months was "too ambitious" and instead sent a group notification letter to all countries, the mainstream of the Platform B comment area would appreciate Leader A's pragmatic correction of mistakes and the ability to correct mistakes after knowing them. They believed that abandoning one-by-one negotiations was a wise and responsible strategic contraction.

Within about a month after the cutoff, just a few days after they had reconciled with Country X, Leader A turned around and threatened to add 50% to all products of Regional Organization A. Official A said that he wanted to "light a fire", and Platform B would gloat and watch Country Y and Regional Organization A pinch each other, joking that "50% of the money will go to his little brother."

Within about a month after the cutoff, when the Court of Appeal reinstated tariffs without giving a single reason, Official C said that even if they lost the case, they would still impose tariffs in a different way. Platform B would ridicule that this was "a formality" and look at the weak employment and profit data of the same day Institution L2 to ridicule that the economy could no longer bear it.

About a month after the cutoff, in response to Institution M's first direct confrontation and public naming of Country Y as a "serious violation" and City G's truce, the mainstream of Platform B's comment area would in turn criticize Institution M for being too impulsive and worry that head-on confrontation would completely break down the negotiations, calling on Country X to take a step back in exchange for relaxation.

Within about a month after the cutoff, 50% of the Country Z steel and aluminum tariffs took effect on time in the early morning, and nearly a hundred years of Company Y shipments to Country Y were suspended every week. Platform B Hot Comments used this scene to ridicule that "it is the industrial chain that is hurt first, not the opponent", and the increase in the price of aluminum cans in breweries was used as a living example of "who will ultimately pay for the tariffs."

Within about two months after the cutoff, the tone of the Leader A and Leader B calls was set to be "very positive", and then the City J negotiations were arranged. Public opinion in Platform B would turn to be highly optimistic. The mainstream believed that the tariff knot was about to be solved at once, and the rare earth and tariff issues would be settled in one fell swoop at the City J talks.

Within about two months after the cutoff, regarding the Country B120 %, 40% transshipment goods, and Country Y zero-tariff agreement, the first reaction in the Platform B comment area was "The 40% transshipment clause is clearly for Country X re-export."
